concept: A little one discovers their baby sibling is sick and leads the whole family in a song about how to take care of someone who doesn't feel well — with rest, soup, and hugs.
learning_objective: Children learn 4 basic sick-care behaviors: rest in bed, drink warm soup, give a hug, and get lots of love.
emotional_objective: Children experience that being sick is scary but love and care make everything better, and they are always safe.

characters.name: Gigi
characters.description: 3-year-old girl with brown pigtails, pink star pajamas, curious and loving

characters.name: Boo
characters.description: Baby sibling toddler, round face, big eyes, blue onesie, expressive

characters.description: Warm nurturing mother, brown hair, soft colors, appears in comfort scenes

characters.name: Pip
characters.description: Small stuffed brown bear, Gigi's comfort toy, held by Boo when sick

song.title: What Should We Do? (The Feel Better Song)

structure.lyrics: (Instrumental — cheerful piano, birds chirping, soft humming)

Oh someone woke up in the morning light
And tip-toed down the hall just right
They peeked inside and what did they see?
The little one was sick as could be!

There in bed with a red little nose
All wrapped up tight from head to toes
Achoo! Achoo! A great big sneeze
"Oh someone come, come help me please!"

What should we do? What should we do?
Someone doesn't feel well today!
What should we do? What should we do?
We're going to make it okay!

Rest in bed, drink some soup
Give a hug, feel better soon!
What should we do? What should we do?
We'll take care of you!

They got a blanket soft and warm
And tucked the little one snug from the storm
Said "I'll bring you something good to eat!"
A warm bowl of soup — a yummy treat!

Then someone came with the gentlest face
And kissed a forehead in the sweetest place
"Rest your eyes," they sang a song
"We're right here, and we love you strong"

What should we do? What should we do?
Someone doesn't feel well today!
What should we do? What should we do?
We're going to make it okay!

Rest in bed, drink some soup
Give a hug, feel better soon!
What should we do? What should we do?
We'll take care of you!

Close your eyes, little one
Feeling sick is no fun
But we're here by your side
Love so warm, love so wide

Sleep and rest, you'll feel better, it's true
We're going to take good care of you
We're all here and we love you too
We love you... we love you...

The sunshine came through the window bright
The little one slowly opened their eyes
"I feel a little better!" they said with a smile
"You'll be well again in just a while!"

The little one wiggled their toes with delight
Achoo! — one last sneeze, but they felt alright!
Everyone laughed and clapped with glee
"You're getting better! Now I can see!"

We knew what to do! We knew what to do!
Someone's feeling better today!
We knew what to do! We knew what to do!
We made the sick go away!

Rest in bed, drank some soup
Got a hug, felt better soon!
We knew what to do! We knew what to do!
We took care of you!

They hugged so nice and tight
"Now you're feeling alright!"
"Thank you, thank you, my dear friend
For taking care of me — right to the end!"

When someone you love doesn't feel well today
You know just what to do, you know what to say
Rest and soup and hugs are the way
And love makes the sick go away!

(Fade out with cheerful instrumental, giggles)

suno_prompt.style_prompt: gentle upbeat children's nursery rhyme, warm piano melody, bright ukulele strums, soft hand percussion, tender female lead vocalist with nurturing quality, warm kids choir on chorus, clear diction for toddlers, 100 bpm verse 85 bpm bridge, C major, lullaby feel in bridge section, cheerful resolution in final chorus, acoustic instruments, no distortion, no minor chords, soothing and safe, toddler-friendly, catchy repeating hook, whimsical bells on chorus, warm reverb, clean mix, emotional arc from worried to happy
suno_prompt.vocal_prompt: female lead voice age 5-7, clear and bright, warm kids choir on choruses, nurturing and safe
suno_prompt.lyrics_for_suno: See suno/sick-song-suno-prompt.md for complete formatted version
suno_prompt.negative_prompt: no adult voice, no minor chords, no distortion, no rap, no heavy bass, no dark tones

thumbnail.concept: Two young sibling characters side-by-side, both waving and smiling big, baby's red nose gone, hearts and sparkles around them
thumbnail.character_expression: Older sibling: big triumphant smile. Baby: laughing, fully recovered.
thumbnail.design_brief: Bright yellow background. Both characters center-left. Text 'FEEL BETTER!' in bold yellow with pink outline, right side. Hearts and sparkle effects. Both faces must be clear and expressive at thumbnail size (1280x720). Small red heart above 'FEEL BETTER!' text. Channel logo bottom-right. Characters should take up 60% of frame. Expression is pure joy — the 'after' moment.

metadata.youtube_description:
🌟 What Should We Do? | The Feel Better Song | Gigi's Playhouse 🌟

The little one doesn't feel well today! Oh no! But don't worry — we know just what to do! Join us as we sing about how to take care of someone who's sick. Rest in bed, drink some yummy soup, get lots of hugs — and most importantly, love makes everything better!

🎵 This fun and caring song teaches toddlers:
✅ What to do when someone feels sick
✅ How to show you care (rest, soup, hugs, love)
✅ That being sick is okay — you'll feel better!
✅ Empathy and caring for others

Sing along with the catchy chorus: "What should we do? What should we do?"

🌈 Perfect for:
👶 Toddlers ages 2-5
👨‍👩‍👧 Families dealing with a sick day
🏫 Preschool and daycare
😴 Quiet time viewing
❤️ Building empathy in young children

📌 Key moments:
0:20 - The little one is sick!
0:55 - "What should we do?" chorus
2:20 - Cozy bridge: lullaby moment
2:50 - Feeling better!
3:25 - Celebration chorus!
